mappings.note: Plot a bar magnet's field lines, sketch the pattern with directions, and say which of two regions is stronger from line closeness - LO-6 in full, both of its clauses.
Names and states the right-hand thumb rule and then applies it to a circular loop (LO-5), on top of the straight conductor's field-pattern activity (LO-4).
Identify four patterns: bar magnet and solenoid are LO-6's two named objects; straight conductor and circular loop are LO-4's.
Draw the solenoid's field lines and read the parallel internal lines as a uniform field (LO-6), plus what that field is used for (LO-4).
Factors setting a current-carrying conductor's field (LO-4) and the right-hand thumb rule that reverses the lines with the current (LO-5).
Part (a) is Fleming's left-hand rule on a moving charge and part (c) is the right-hand thumb rule (LO-5); part (b) draws a circular loop's lines (LO-4); the deflected particle is the LO-1 force.
Magnetic force defined and its dependence on the current and field directions (LO-1), with Fleming's left-hand rule named and explained (LO-5).
Draw the field lines of a circular coil and name two factors for its magnitude (LO-4); the opening 'what are field lines, how is the direction determined' is LO-6.

The Oersted-and-Ampere passage is never assessed: both sub-questions ask what a magnetic needle is and why a suspended magnet sets north-south, i.e. earth's magnetism, for which the frame has no outcome. Goal level; frame gap and a stem/question mismatch both recorded.
Ionic currents in nerve cells produce a magnetic field - LO-4's 'a current produces a field' premise, applied to the body.

State the right-hand thumb rule and apply it under a power line (LO-5); the B-versus-distance curve on a circular coil's axis is LO-4; part (iv), the force on an east-west conductor in the earth's field, is LO-1.
All five sub-questions are bar-magnet field-line convention, crowding and pole strength - LO-6 alone.
Earth wire on a metal-bodied appliance, the three wires, and the earth as a conductor - LO-7.

Mobile-phone microwave radiation, skull absorption and brain heating. Nothing here is magnetism; no outcome in this frame fits and the item does not belong in this chapter. Goal level, and recorded as out-of-scope content.

The passage is domestic wiring (LO-7), but all four sub-questions are P = VI, I = P/V, E = Pt and R = V/I computations, which belong to C 2.4's mathematisation and have no outcome inside this chapter's frame.
The compass sets perpendicular to the current because the field is circular (LO-4); reversing the current turns it through 180 degrees by the right-hand thumb rule (LO-5).
All four sub-questions are field-line direction inside the magnet, crowding at the poles, closed curves and non-intersection - LO-6.
Sub-questions (ii)-(iv) read a bar magnet's strength off its field lines (LO-6); (v) is Oersted's current-makes-a-field discovery (LO-4). Sub-question (i), the SI unit, has no outcome - recorded.
